**My reasoning, as this farmer:**

I have been farming this land since I was a boy helping my father. I know this county's soil and weather. In Quzhou, everyone does wheat and maize — one after the other on the same ground. The wheat goes in October, we harvest it in June, and the maize goes straight in. That is what the land is for. I would not change to vegetables or cotton because I do not know those markets and I have no connections to sell them. Wheat and maize I can sell to the grain station — simple, reliable.

I have about 10 mu of land, all flat. I will plant wheat on all of it for winter, then turn it straight to maize in summer on the same plots.

For wheat seed I buy the improved variety from the village co-op — Jimai or something similar they have in stock. Not the old traditional seed, but I do not trust whatever the newest experimental hybrid is either. The improved one gives me a safe yield.

For maize I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid. Every man in my village uses it. It is consistent. I am not going to experiment.

Fertilizer: I put nitrogen heavy on wheat — that is what makes the heads fill. My father did it, I do it. Three irrigations on wheat — before winter freeze, at jointing, at heading. Water is from the well and it costs money and time, so three is enough. Maize I irrigate once if it is a dry year — summer rain usually handles it.

I spray pesticide twice on each crop. Aphids on wheat, corn borer on maize — I watch for them and spray when I see them or when neighbors say they are spreading.

I do rotary tillage on the wheat ground before planting. For maize after wheat harvest, I seed directly without ploughing — saves time and the soil is already loose.
